name: Data
question: Is my data usable for property to structure design?
purpose: Check the uploaded data before any training: how well posed the inverse problem is, whether each target has support, and whether anything new can be reached at all.
verdict_rule: the worst grade of its graded metrics
caveats: S0 FAILs on Perov-5 for all configurations. That is a property of the dataset, not of the pipeline: it is a complete grid with 96% zero gaps. It is reported, not hidden.

metrics.name: Materials sharing a property profile
metrics.definition: Share of materials whose rounded property vector is shared by at least 9 others.
metrics.meaning_good: Properties mostly identify a material, so a target has few possible answers.
metrics.meaning_bad: Many different materials have the same properties: property to structure has no unique answer, only a distribution of answers.
metrics.remedy: Add another property column (more properties separate more materials), or accept a set of candidates rather than one.
metrics.recalibrated: Was bundled with the zero share into one 'zero-inflation' check, which warned on the MP dataset for having 53% zero gaps even though its inverse problem is well posed (0% shared profiles). Zero share is now context; this is the graded part.

metrics.name: Zero share of the target property
metrics.definition: Share of training materials whose target property is exactly zero.
metrics.remedy: Context for the metal/non-metal metric in S1 and for how many targets are reachable.

metrics.name: Training support at a target
metrics.definition: Number of training materials within +-0.25 of the requested target value.
metrics.meaning_good: Enough neighbours for the model to have learned this region.
metrics.meaning_bad: Almost nothing in the data resembles the request, so labels there are extrapolation.
metrics.remedy: Drop the target, or add data in that range.
metrics.reference_note: Perov-5: 10936 at 0 eV; 56 at 2 eV; 22 at 4 eV; 8 at 5 eV (the last two FAIL).

metrics.name: Distinct compositions per element
metrics.definition: Mean number of distinct compositions each element appears in, across the training split.
metrics.meaning_good: Each element is seen in enough different compounds for the decoder to learn it.
metrics.meaning_bad: The decoder cannot learn a reliable latent to element mapping; generation will not work and the run must use screening.
metrics.remedy: Use screening mode:  python -m meidnet_eval.screen_local <intake> --ckpt MODEL.pt --family FAMILY[:variant] --gap COLUMN --targets ...  (enumerates the family, labels every composition from its template structure, judges independently); or add data.
metrics.computed_by: measured in the density experiment; computed by intake.py in the preview
metrics.reference_note: Trained identically on Perov-5 subsets: 12 -> 0.1%, 30 -> 0.7%, 80 -> 5.4%, 218 -> 64% composition recovery (journal Entry 44), so this predicts S3 before training.

metrics.name: Share of the design space absent from the data
metrics.definition: Fraction of the charge-balanced design space built from the data's own chemistry that the data does not already contain.
metrics.meaning_good: There is unexplored space to search.
metrics.meaning_bad: The dataset has already explored its own design space, so anything 'novel' requires chemistry the model has never seen.
metrics.remedy: Enlarge the design space (more prototypes, more anion sets), not the element list.
metrics.reference_note: Perov-5 is a complete 52x52x7 grid: 0 of 148 novel candidates avoided unseen elements (journal Entry 40). The MP set leaves 63% of its space unexplored.

components.note: ingest_upload.py (upload adapter: folder + spreadsheet -> one table, joined on the file name, every unmatched row reported)
preview.py (the gate: runs with no model)
screen_local.py (screening mode on a laptop: enumerate the family, label every composition from its template cell, judge independently)
auto_family.py (design space learned from the data)
